title: Cahal Pech settled
description: The hilltop site above the Macal River is first occupied, one of the oldest recognisably Maya settlements in Belize.

title: Caracol defeats Tikal
description: Caracol wins a ‘star war’ over Tikal, the greatest city of the region, and rises to dominate the Maya lowlands for over a century.

title: Shipwrecked sailors settle
place: Belize River (mouth; shown at Belize City)
description: Shipwrecked English sailors make the first recorded British settlement on the coast, the origin of the logwood-cutting Baymen.

title: Treaty of Madrid
description: Spain recognises British possessions in the Americas, the basis on which Britain later defends the Bay settlements.

title: Convention of London
description: Spain confirms the Baymen's right to cut logwood between the Sibun and Hondo rivers in exchange for their withdrawal from the Mosquito Shore.

title: Battle of St. George's Caye
description: Baymen and their slaves defeat a Spanish fleet off the caye, the decisive fight later celebrated as the nation's founding battle.

title: Treaty with Guatemala
description: Britain and Guatemala fix the boundaries of the settlement; Guatemala's later reading of the treaty seeds the territorial claim.

title: British Honduras declared a colony
description: The Crown formally declares the settlement a British colony, subordinate at first to the governor of Jamaica.

title: Crown colony in its own right
description: British Honduras is made a crown colony independent of Jamaica.

title: Belize City hurricane
description: A hurricane strikes on the battle anniversary it interrupts, destroying most of Belize City and killing well over a thousand people.

title: Soberanis labour movement
description: Antonio Soberanis leads marches and a sit-down strike by the unemployed, the start of organised labour in the colony.

title: PUP founded
description: The People's United Party is founded and begins the campaign for self-government and independence.

title: Hurricane Hattie
description: Hurricane Hattie kills hundreds and wrecks Belize City, prompting the building of a new capital inland.

title: Belmopan becomes the capital
description: The government moves inland to the new hurricane-sheltered capital of Belmopan.

title: Name changed to Belize
description: The colony is renamed Belize as independence, delayed by Guatemala's claim, nevertheless nears.

title: Independence
description: Belize becomes independent with a British garrison staying on against a Guatemalan invasion threat.

title: Unrest
description: Protests and riots over tax rises and graft paralyse the country in its worst unrest since independence.

title: Referendum votes for the ICJ
description: Voters agree to send Guatemala's territorial claim to the International Court of Justice.
